offence_severity: Minimum/Maximum: 7 years to life imprisonment (prior to 2013 amendment)
physical_harm: Rape resulting in torn hymen and swelling, but no external injuries
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of prosecutrix (PW-1) is supported by medical evidence and also by the evidence of PW-4, who saw the accused running away from the scene of occurrence.
witness_credibility: The oral testimony of the prosecutrix that she was subjected to rape cannot be ignored, even in the absence of external injury.

legal_representation.state: Ms. Swarupama Chaturvedi, B. N. Dubey, Ms. Devika Gulati, Ms. Vaishali Verma, Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered on 10th March, 1993; medical examination conducted on 9th March, 1993; charge sheet filed; trial completed

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Section 376 IPC and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment
appeal_history.high_court: Reversed conviction and acquitted the respondent-accused
appeal_history.supreme_court: Set aside High Court's judgment and restored trial court's conviction, reducing sentence to four years

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the evidence of the prosecutrix (PW-1) is supported by medical evidence and the testimony of PW-4, who saw the accused running away from the scene. The delay in registration of the FIR was properly explained.
defence_argument: The defence, through the High Court, argued that the absence of external injuries on the prosecutrix indicated her consent for the sexual intercourse and that the delay in registration of the FIR was a valid reason for acquitting the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the absence of external injuries on the victim of rape does not lead to an inference that the accused did not commit forcible sexual intercourse, and that the oral testimony of the prosecutrix cannot be ignored.
precedent_relied_upon: B.C. Deva @ Dyava v. State of Karnataka (2007) 12 SCC 122 : [2007] 8 SCR 509
sentencing_rationale: The sentence of imprisonment of seven years imposed on the respondent was reduced to four years due to the passage of time and the discretion vested with the Court under the proviso to Section 376(1) IPC prior to the 2013 amendment.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The passage of time since the occurrence (about 25 years) and the discretion vested with the Court under the proviso to Section 376(1) IPC prior to the 2013 amendment.
other_sentence_order: The respondent is to surrender to custody within a period of four weeks from today to serve the remaining sentence, if not already undergone.
